source: Cox & D'Antonio 3e Table 6.3, PDF page 251 (printed p. 194)
about: Rendered PDF page 251, folio 194 (running head "194 Acoustic Absorbers and Diffusers"); the table occupies the top half, followed by the prose of Section 6.4.1 (temperature correction, Equations 6.7 and 6.8) and the start of Section 6.4.2 Open porosity. Title as printed: "Table 6.3 Typical fibre diameters reported in various acoustic studies". Two columns, headings in italic: "Material" and "Diameter (μm)". The table has NO section headings; the rows are alphabetical and thin horizontal rules are drawn after every fourth row (after Coir, Graphite, Kevlar and Ramie), a typographic aid only, so no group field is given. No footnotes. Every material name carries at least one superscript reference number into the chapter 6 reference list (PDF pages 276-281, printed pp. 219-224). The page before (PDF 249, printed p. 192) refers to the table twice: "For mineral and glass fibre, see Table 6.3 for typical diameters" (after Bies and Hansen's fibreglass relation, Equation 6.5, which needs the fibre radius a) and "These formulations often require the radius of the fibres, and Table 6.3 gives some indicative values for different materials." Printed unit is micrometres, the library unit, so every number is carried over with factor 1. Ranges printed with an en dash go to ranges; the two cells that list a range and a separate value with a comma (Polypropylene "5–25, 63", Wool "14, 37–63") go to reported. Note that the table gives fibre DIAMETERS while Equation 6.5 and the Table 6.4 formulae use the fibre RADIUS.
